scope: Every status below refers to the Orna engine, not Python reference checks.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONF-001
tests.obligation: A conformance claim MUST identify its classes, implementation version and exact specification publication digest.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONF-002
tests.obligation: A claim MUST distinguish supported optional profiles from mandatory facilities and list the implementation tests actually executed.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONF-003
tests.obligation: An implementation MUST pass every applicable conformance fixture and behavioural test before claiming the corresponding class. A parsed example is not proof of type correctness or runtime behaviour.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONF-004
tests.obligation: Extensions MUST NOT change the meaning of valid source, repository trees or protocol messages in the claimed profile.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONF-006
tests.obligation: A full-runtime claim MUST execute the assertion, automatic-failure, recovery, conversion, transaction, cancellation and cross-table validation scenarios applicable to it.

tests.subject: ORNA-CLOSURE-004
tests.obligation: Configuration options MUST NOT change the language, identity, transaction, checkpoint or repository semantics specified here. Resource limits and presentation preferences may vary only where explicitly permitted and must remain observable.

tests.subject: ORNA-SOURCE-001
tests.obligation: The parser MUST expose distinct entrypoints for module units and row units.

tests.subject: ORNA-SOURCE-002
tests.obligation: A module unit MUST contain declarations only at top level.

tests.subject: ORNA-SOURCE-003
tests.obligation: A row unit MUST contain exactly one record expression and MUST NOT contain declarations.

tests.subject: ORNA-NS-001
tests.obligation: A directory's `main.orna` MUST define that directory's namespace.

tests.subject: ORNA-NS-002
tests.obligation: A non-`main.orna` module filename MUST add its stem as the final namespace component.

tests.subject: ORNA-NS-003
tests.obligation: The repository root `main.orna` MUST define the root namespace.

tests.subject: ORNA-NS-004
tests.obligation: A repository MUST NOT contain both `x.orna` and `x/main.orna` where both would define the same namespace.

tests.subject: ORNA-NS-005
tests.obligation: `sys` and `std` are the only reserved top-level namespaces.

tests.subject: ORNA-NS-006
tests.obligation: `sys` MUST be built into every conforming implementation and MUST NOT be replaced or shadowed.

tests.subject: ORNA-NS-007
tests.obligation: `std` MUST remain optional and replaceable, although its top-level name is reserved when present.

tests.subject: ORNA-IMPORT-001
tests.obligation: `use a.b;` MUST make namespace `a.b` available under its final component unless it conflicts.

tests.subject: ORNA-IMPORT-002
tests.obligation: `use a.b as x;` MUST make the imported namespace available as `x`.

tests.subject: ORNA-IMPORT-003
tests.obligation: `use a.b.*;` MUST import all public names from `a.b` into the current lexical scope.

tests.subject: ORNA-IMPORT-004
tests.obligation: `use a.b.{X, y};` MUST import only the named public definitions.

tests.subject: ORNA-IMPORT-005
tests.obligation: `use x as _;` MUST import the prelude set explicitly exported by that pinned module, without binding a namespace alias. An absent prelude declaration imports no names; it does not mean wildcard import.

tests.subject: ORNA-LEX-001
tests.obligation: Orna source MUST be UTF-8.

tests.subject: ORNA-LEX-002
tests.obligation: Implementations MUST preserve enough source position information to report line, column and byte-span diagnostics.

tests.subject: ORNA-LEX-003
tests.obligation: Line comments begin with `//` and end at the line ending.

tests.subject: ORNA-LEX-004
tests.obligation: Block comments use `/* ... */` and MUST support nesting; delimiters inside a string literal do not start comments.

tests.subject: ORNA-LEX-005
tests.obligation: Implementations MUST compare identifiers using Unicode NFC normalization while preserving original spelling for display.

tests.subject: ORNA-LEX-006
tests.obligation: Namespace and definition-name comparison MUST be case-sensitive.

tests.subject: ORNA-LEX-007
tests.obligation: The exact keyword set is `as`, `assert`, `base`, `break`, `case`, `continue`, `dim`, `else`, `enum`, `false`, `fn`, `for`, `if`, `impl`, `in`, `let`, `loop`, `null`, `offset`, `affine`, `protocol`, `pub`, `return`, `self`, `static`, `table`, `true`, `type`, `unit`, `use`, and `while`. Literal markers such as T, Z and f are not standalone reserved identifiers. Contextual names follow the rules below.

tests.subject: ORNA-LEX-008
tests.obligation: `Some` and payload-free option `null` are core option-value spellings. `Result`, `Ok`, and `Err` are not core 1.0 type or variant spellings. User enum variants remain namespace-qualified in patterns unless explicitly imported; a bare identifier pattern otherwise introduces a binding.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIT-001
tests.obligation: Integer source numerals have arbitrary-precision parse semantics and are range-checked when checked against a bounded integer type.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIT-002
tests.obligation: An unsuffixed fractional or exponent numeral is represented exactly during parsing and defaults to `Decimal` when no expected numeric type exists. It MAY be checked against an expected `Float` type, in which case conversion to IEEE-754 binary64 uses correctly rounded round-to-nearest, ties-to-even semantics. The `f` suffix explicitly selects `Float`.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIT-003
tests.obligation: `.decimal` explicitly selects `Decimal`. Money and exact quantity contexts MUST NOT silently infer an intermediate binary `Float`.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIT-004
tests.obligation: String interpolation expressions use `{ expression }` within a double-quoted string.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIT-005
tests.obligation: Date and instant literals use ISO-8601-compatible forms. In a contiguous token sequence matching a complete date or instant literal, the lexer MUST recognize that literal before considering the characters as separate integer and subtraction tokens.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIT-006
tests.obligation: Decimal, Float, Date and Instant token classes MUST be disjoint after lexical classification; a conforming lexer MUST NOT emit two different tokenizations for the same complete source numeral.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIT-007
tests.obligation: `decimal_expression.CurrencyType` constructs exact `Money<CurrencyType>` only when the selected nominal type implements `Currency`; it is not a general implicit conversion or a special `currency` declaration.

tests.subject: ORNA-PATTERN-001
tests.obligation: In a record pattern only, a bare field name is shorthand for a same-named binding: `{ count }` is exactly `{ count: count }`. This shorthand destructures an existing field; it does not construct a record and does not permit record-literal punning.

tests.subject: ORNA-PATTERN-002
tests.obligation: A record-pattern field written `name: pattern` matches field `name` and applies the nested pattern. Construction always uses explicit `name: expression`, while destructuring MAY use the shorthand from ORNA-PATTERN-001.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYNTAX-001
tests.obligation: Construction MUST check each supplied field once in written order, reject duplicates/unknown fields, apply defaults once and enforce visibility and refinements. Private fields cannot be bypassed by constructing a record with matching names.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYNTAX-002
tests.obligation: A processor MUST use the pinned lexical profile, validate calendar/scalar values after tokenisation, and report byte spans without reinterpreting malformed tokens as another expression.

tests.subject: ORNA-TYPE-002
tests.obligation: A failable expression has a successful value type and a separate abrupt failure channel carrying an `Error`; failure is not represented by `Result<T, E>` in source.

tests.subject: ORNA-TYPE-003
tests.obligation: Automatic failure propagation MUST NOT silently discard a stream item. Stream retry, preservation, skip and dead-letter behavior remains explicit through the stream/checkpoint model.

tests.subject: ORNA-TYPE-004
tests.obligation: Implementations MUST NOT use the same type name for raw bytes and a byte-count quantity.

tests.subject: ORNA-TYPE-005
tests.obligation: User-defined closed variants use nominal `enum` declarations. Orna does not use the expression-pipeline token `|` as a type-union or variant-list operator.

tests.subject: ORNA-TYPE-006
tests.obligation: `Result`, `Ok`, and `Err` are not reserved core type constructors or variants in 1.0.

tests.subject: ORNA-TYPE-007
tests.obligation: A user-defined `type` declaration is either a transparent alias, a nominal type, or a refined nominal type as specified in [aliases, nominal types and refinements](#expressions).

tests.subject: ORNA-TYPE-008
tests.obligation: The absence of a source annotation does not make a value dynamically typed. A conforming processor MUST infer a static type or issue a type-inference diagnostic.

tests.subject: ORNA-VALUE-001
tests.obligation: Primitive, list, record, enum, option, quantity, money, nominal and row values MUST have value semantics.

tests.subject: ORNA-VALUE-002
tests.obligation: A row returned from a query is an immutable snapshot containing its table identity, primary key, snapshot context and logical fields. A later table update MUST NOT mutate an already-held row value.

tests.subject: ORNA-VALUE-003
tests.obligation: Closures capture values at creation time. Table handles retain their database/snapshot context unless the program explicitly selects another context.

tests.subject: ORNA-VALUE-004
tests.obligation: Cyclic ordinary list/record/nominal values are not constructible in version 1.0. Persistent graph cycles may exist through table references.

tests.subject: ORNA-VALUE-005
tests.obligation: Memory management, pointer identity and finalization timing MUST NOT be observable language semantics.

tests.subject: ORNA-NUM-001
tests.obligation: `Int` MUST represent exact integers.

tests.subject: ORNA-NUM-002
tests.obligation: `Decimal` MUST represent finite exact base-10 values with implementation resource limits but without binary-float conversion.

tests.subject: ORNA-FLOAT-003
tests.obligation: `Float` MUST NOT be accepted as a primary-key component or default hash-key type.

tests.subject: ORNA-FLOAT-004
tests.obligation: Float arithmetic MUST NOT be silently reassociated or evaluated with unspecified fast-math transformations.

tests.subject: ORNA-FLOAT-005
tests.obligation: A Float aggregate MUST process rows in the relation's observable order. Empty `sum` returns additive zero; empty `min`, `max` and `mean` return `null`.

tests.subject: ORNA-FLOAT-007
tests.obligation: For a non-empty Float input, `min` and `max` return the canonical NaN if any input is NaN. Otherwise they use numeric order, with `min` choosing `-0.0` when either zero sign is present and `max` choosing `+0.0`. Libraries MAY provide explicitly named finite-only or NaN-ignoring alternatives.

tests.subject: ORNA-TIME-001
tests.obligation: Telemetry timestamps SHOULD use `Instant`.

tests.subject: ORNA-TIME-002
tests.obligation: Calendar-day operations over `Instant` values MUST require or derive an explicit time zone.

tests.subject: ORNA-TIME-004
tests.obligation: Fixed elapsed-time windows and calendar periods MUST be distinct operations even if their textual durations appear similar.

tests.subject: ORNA-RANGE-001
tests.obligation: `a..b` constructs a half-open range containing values `x` for which `a <= x && x < b`.

tests.subject: ORNA-RANGE-002
tests.obligation: `a..=b` constructs an inclusive range containing values `x` for which `a <= x && x <= b`.

tests.subject: ORNA-RANGE-003
tests.obligation: Either endpoint MAY be omitted where the surrounding operation supplies a type and meaningful unbounded side.

tests.subject: ORNA-RANGE-004
tests.obligation: Range endpoints MUST have one compatible ordered type. Empty ranges are valid ordinary values.

tests.subject: ORNA-RANGE-005
tests.obligation: Ranges have a total order only when `T` has a total order: lower endpoint (unbounded first), then upper endpoint (unbounded last), then exclusivity before inclusivity at equal endpoints. This ordering is for sorting/serialization and does not imply overlap uniqueness.

tests.subject: ORNA-RANGE-006
tests.obligation: `value in range` tests membership. Range iteration/slicing behavior is supplied by the relevant iterable/index operation rather than by special grammar.

tests.subject: ORNA-RANGE-007
tests.obligation: Version 1.0 does not redefine primary-key equality as range overlap. Temporal exclusion/non-overlap constraints are represented by explicit table or cross-table assertions, not by making overlap masquerade as equality.

tests.subject: ORNA-UNIT-004
tests.obligation: Adding quantities of incompatible dimensions is a compile-time error where types are known.

tests.subject: ORNA-UNIT-006
tests.obligation: Integration reduces dimensions algebraically; integrating speed over time yields length.

tests.subject: ORNA-UNIT-008
tests.obligation: Unit suffix resolution MUST be static and unambiguous in the current import context. A unit suffix does not perform an arbitrary `From` conversion.

tests.subject: ORNA-MONEY-002
tests.obligation: Two amounts with different currency parameters MUST NOT be added without an explicit data-backed conversion.

tests.subject: ORNA-INFER-008
tests.obligation: Contextual numeric and collection inference MUST preserve the exactness rules of [numeric exactness](#types) and [literal forms](#lexical).

tests.subject: ORNA-INFER-009
tests.obligation: Protocol selection and nested implementations participate in inference, but overlapping implementations remain invalid.

tests.subject: ORNA-NOMINAL-001
tests.obligation: `type Name = Existing;` declares a transparent alias with no new runtime or equality identity.

tests.subject: ORNA-NOMINAL-002
tests.obligation: `type Name { ... }` declares a nominal type distinct from every structural record with the same fields.

tests.subject: ORNA-NOMINAL-003
tests.obligation: `type Name = Base { ... }` declares a refined nominal type represented by `Base` and distinct from `Base`.

tests.subject: ORNA-NOMINAL-004
tests.obligation: Orna 1.0 has no separate `opaque` type declaration.

tests.subject: ORNA-NOMINAL-009
tests.obligation: Nominal equality, order, hashing, display, presentation and codec behavior are supplied by explicit core rules or protocol implementations; structural coincidence alone does not grant them.

tests.subject: ORNA-NOMINAL-010
tests.obligation: A formatter SHOULD keep nested implementations adjacent to the type whose representation they can access.

tests.subject: ORNA-REFINE-004
tests.obligation: The removed `where self` spelling is invalid and receives `ORNA-A091-001`.

tests.subject: ORNA-REFINE-005
tests.obligation: Refined-type assertions are enforced in all build and runtime modes; they are not debug-only.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONVERT-009
tests.obligation: A conversion implementation may access private fields of its target because it is lexically owned by that target.

tests.subject: ORNA-INFER-012
tests.obligation: Refactoring a private helper from an explicit type to an equivalent inferred type MUST NOT change exported semantic identity by itself.

tests.subject: ORNA-INFER-014
tests.obligation: Historical execution uses the inferred signatures captured by the historical code snapshot, not signatures re-inferred from current source.

tests.subject: ORNA-IMPL-003
tests.obligation: Nested implementations are not allowed inside a transparent alias because the alias has no separate nominal ownership.

tests.subject: ORNA-IMPL-004
tests.obligation: A refined nominal type MAY contain nested implementations in the same body as its assertions.

tests.subject: ORNA-MODULE-001
tests.obligation: Arbitrary expression statements MUST NOT appear at module top level.

tests.subject: ORNA-MODULE-002
tests.obligation: A module-scope `assert` is permitted only as the cross-table invariant form specified in [the tables chapter](#tables). It is not arbitrary module-load execution.

tests.subject: ORNA-MODULE-003
tests.obligation: Loading source parses, resolves, infers and type-checks declarations and assertion plans; it never starts streams, performs external work or mutates current table state.

tests.subject: ORNA-FN-001
tests.obligation: Calling a function MUST evaluate it at the time of the call against supplied values and the current database context.

tests.subject: ORNA-FN-002
tests.obligation: A qualified function name without call parentheses denotes the function value and MUST NOT invoke it.

tests.subject: ORNA-FN-003
tests.obligation: Merely naming a function in the REPL MUST inspect the function and MUST NOT call it.

tests.subject: ORNA-FN-004
tests.obligation: A function declaration MUST NOT imply persisted materialization of its result.

tests.subject: ORNA-FN-005
tests.obligation: A function value has a statically known inferred or annotated parameter/return signature and may be stored in a local value, passed as an argument or returned from another function.

tests.subject: ORNA-FN-008
tests.obligation: Parameters and return types MAY omit annotations where inference succeeds.

tests.subject: ORNA-FN-009
tests.obligation: Every reachable return path and block tail contributes to return-type inference.

tests.subject: ORNA-FN-011
tests.obligation: Merely declaring a function does not execute its body or its assertions.

tests.subject: ORNA-FN-012
tests.obligation: Public functions SHOULD use explicit boundary annotations when those improve API stability, documentation or diagnostics; this is guidance, not a requirement to annotate ordinary code.

tests.subject: ORNA-ENUM-001
tests.obligation: An enum is nominal and closed to variants declared in its body.

tests.subject: ORNA-ENUM-002
tests.obligation: A payload-free variant is referenced as `Enum.variant`.

tests.subject: ORNA-ENUM-003
tests.obligation: A payload variant uses a record payload and is constructed with explicit named fields, for example `SyncResult.ok { count: 3 }`. Destructuring uses record-pattern semantics, including the pattern-only shorthand `SyncResult.ok { count }`; construction does not permit that shorthand.

tests.subject: ORNA-ENUM-004
tests.obligation: Variant payload field order is source-preserving for presentation and structural for matching.

tests.subject: ORNA-ENUM-005
tests.obligation: A payload-free enum MAY be a primary-key component and is encoded by its canonical variant name. An enum variant carrying a payload MUST NOT be a primary-key component in version 1.0.

tests.subject: ORNA-ENUM-006
tests.obligation: Variant identifiers SHOULD use lowercase `snake_case` for readability, but identifier case remains part of the name.

tests.subject: ORNA-CASE-007
tests.obligation: A processor MUST NOT interpret `case` as exception handling. It is ordinary exhaustive value branching; failures are handled by `|?`.

tests.subject: ORNA-GENERIC-001
tests.obligation: Generic parameters are explicit in public source when a generic abstraction is intended; local type arguments may be inferred.

tests.subject: ORNA-GENERIC-004
tests.obligation: Specialization, associated types, higher-kinded types, negative implementations and runtime protocol objects are outside version 1.0.

tests.subject: ORNA-GENERIC-008
tests.obligation: A protocol may declare instance functions and static properties.

tests.subject: ORNA-GENERIC-010
tests.obligation: `static fn` is not a protocol-member category in 1.0. Behavior that does not require an instance is expressed as an ordinary function or as construction/conversion owned by the target type.

tests.subject: ORNA-GENERIC-011
tests.obligation: Every required protocol member must have exactly one compatible implementation in a conforming nested `impl` block.

tests.subject: ORNA-GENERIC-015
tests.obligation: A table declaration MAY contain nested protocol implementations for its nominal row type; those implementations are not stored row fields and do not affect table identity or storage.

tests.subject: ORNA-CFLOW-004
tests.obligation: `case` is an expression and MUST be exhaustive for closed types.

tests.subject: ORNA-CFLOW-007
tests.obligation: `for` consumes a finite `Iterable`. An unbounded `Stream` is consumed by stream operations such as `for_each`.

tests.subject: ORNA-CFLOW-009
tests.obligation: Orna has no implicit truthiness.

tests.subject: ORNA-CFLOW-010
tests.obligation: A braced control-flow expression (`if`, `case`, `for`, `while`, or `loop`) MAY be used as a statement without a trailing semicolon. When it is the final item of a block, it is the block's tail expression unless followed by `;`.

tests.subject: ORNA-PARSE-002
tests.obligation: While parsing a block, a braced control-flow expression followed by another block item is a statement; the final unsemicolonated expression immediately before `}` is the block tail. `loop` used as a non-final statement requires `;` when its value would otherwise be ambiguous.

tests.subject: ORNA-RUN-001
tests.obligation: `orna run <qualified-function>` MUST invoke the named public function.

tests.subject: ORNA-RUN-002
tests.obligation: `orna run` without a function name MUST invoke root `main()` if present and MUST otherwise produce a diagnostic.

tests.subject: ORNA-RUN-003
tests.obligation: A file path MUST NOT acquire special execution behavior merely because it is named `ingest/main.orna` or appears under a particular directory.

tests.subject: ORNA-LAMBDA-002
tests.obligation: Zero or multiple parameters use parentheses.

tests.subject: ORNA-PARSE-001
tests.obligation: When `(` begins an expression, the parser scans to the matching `)` while respecting nested delimiters. If the next significant token is `=>`, the construct is an anonymous-function parameter list; otherwise an empty pair is Unit, a comma at the outermost parenthesis level denotes a tuple, and a nonempty comma-free pair groups one expression. Implementations may use equivalent parsing machinery, but MUST produce the same parse.

tests.subject: ORNA-LAMBDA-003
tests.obligation: Anonymous functions capture immutable lexical values. Such a value is called a closure when it captures at least one surrounding value.

tests.subject: ORNA-PIPE-004
tests.obligation: Any callable may be a success-pipeline stage when its first parameter accepts the piped value. There is no separate pipe-function declaration or category.

tests.subject: ORNA-PIPE-005
tests.obligation: A direct anonymous function used as a pipeline stage MUST be parenthesized:

tests.subject: ORNA-PIPE-006
tests.obligation: Bitwise operations are complete ordinary functions supplied by `std.bits`, such as `bit_or`, `bit_and`, `bit_xor`, `bit_not`, `shift_left` and `shift_right`.

tests.subject: ORNA-PIPE-007
tests.obligation: If evaluation to the left of `|` fails, the stage to its right is not evaluated and the failure continues outward.

tests.subject: ORNA-PIPE-011
tests.obligation: `|` and `|?` associate leftward, permitting readable success/recovery sequences:

tests.subject: ORNA-PIPE-012
tests.obligation: `|?` is ordinary explicit recovery, not assertion syntax and not a stream dead-letter operation.

tests.subject: ORNA-COALESCE-001
tests.obligation: `a ?? b` evaluates `a` first. If `a` is `Some(value)`, it yields that value without evaluating `b`; otherwise it evaluates and yields `b`.

tests.subject: ORNA-COALESCE-002
tests.obligation: `??` associates rightward: `a ?? b ?? c` means `a ?? (b ?? c)`.

tests.subject: ORNA-COMPARE-001
tests.obligation: Equality and comparison operators do not chain. `a < b < c` and `a == b == c` are syntax errors; source writes `a < b && b < c` when that is intended.

tests.subject: ORNA-COMPARE-002
tests.obligation: Comparison operands evaluate left-to-right and each accepted operator yields `Bool`.

tests.subject: ORNA-MEMBER-001
tests.obligation: `value.field` resolves only a field selector declared by the value's nominal/structural type.

tests.subject: ORNA-MEMBER-002
tests.obligation: Every table field generates a first-class selector named `Table.field`. Selecting `row.field` applies that selector to the row.

tests.subject: ORNA-MEMBER-003
tests.obligation: `value.member(args)` is valid only for a member or protocol operation explicitly associated with the receiver type. Importing a free function whose first parameter happens to match MUST NOT silently make it a dot method.

tests.subject: ORNA-MEMBER-004
tests.obligation: Free functions remain ordinary calls and may always be used through the pipeline when argument one is compatible.

tests.subject: ORNA-MEMBER-005
tests.obligation: Core types may define genuine associated members such as relation `count`, `first`, or codec `encode`; this does not create unrestricted UFCS.

tests.subject: ORNA-MEMBER-006
tests.obligation: `Type.static_property` resolves a static property supplied by a protocol implementation and does not require construction of a value.

tests.subject: ORNA-ERR-009
tests.obligation: There is no intrinsic `Result<T,E>`, `Ok(...)` or `Err(...)` failure surface. An unresolved use in that role receives `ORNA091-E-RESULT`. Independently declared user types and variants with these names remain ordinary declarations; this rule does not reserve their names.

tests.subject: ORNA-ERR-010
tests.obligation: Recovery uses `|?`, ordinary functions, `case` over ordinary values, or a combination of them. It does not require a parallel exception syntax.

tests.subject: ORNA-FAILURE-002
tests.obligation: The compiler MUST track whether reachable operations may fail sufficiently to preserve control flow, rollback and diagnostics, without requiring source-visible effect annotations in 1.0.

tests.subject: ORNA-FAILURE-003
tests.obligation: Public metadata SHOULD expose the inferred set of nominal failure types where knowable and `Error` where open-ended.

tests.subject: ORNA-FAILURE-004
tests.obligation: A broad recovery handler receives at least `Error`; a processor MAY infer a narrower nominal error type from the left expression.

tests.subject: ORNA-FAILURE-005
tests.obligation: Error values are ordinary inspectable values when explicitly received by a recovery handler, but they do not become successful results merely because they are values there.

tests.subject: ORNA-FAILURE-007
tests.obligation: Nested `|?` stages handle the nearest failure that reaches them according to left-associative pipeline evaluation.

tests.subject: ORNA-FAILURE-009
tests.obligation: Host boundaries record unhandled errors in `sys.Run`/`sys.Failure` as applicable and present a safe diagnostic.

tests.subject: ORNA-FAILURE-010
tests.obligation: The runtime MUST distinguish an activation failure from a preserved stream-item failure record; the latter is durable administration data produced by checkpoint policy.

tests.subject: ORNA-TABLE-001
tests.obligation: `table` MUST be the only core declaration for persistent relational data.

tests.subject: ORNA-KEY-001
tests.obligation: A table parameter list MUST define the complete primary key in parameter order.

tests.subject: ORNA-KEY-002
tests.obligation: Primary-key fields MUST be visible as ordinary logical row fields even when a virtual/interchange row document obtains its key from a schema-aware path. Canonical persisted rows retain the complete key in the primary index.

tests.subject: ORNA-AUTOID-001
tests.obligation: A table without explicit key parameters MUST receive an implicit monotonically increasing `Int` key named `id`.

tests.subject: ORNA-AUTOID-005
tests.obligation: A committed snapshot MUST include the allocator watermark known at that snapshot for historical introspection.

tests.subject: ORNA-AUTOID-006
tests.obligation: Independent offline clones have independent allocators and MAY allocate the same integer. A merge of different rows with the same automatic ID MUST create a typed row conflict and MUST NOT silently renumber either row or its references.

tests.subject: ORNA-KEYDEF-002
tests.obligation: A supplied key MUST bypass its default expression.

tests.subject: ORNA-KEYDEF-004
tests.obligation: Key defaults that inspect current table state are allocation logic, not deterministic pure identities. Independent branches MAY allocate colliding or different keys; semantic merge MUST report resulting conflicts honestly.

tests.subject: ORNA-FIELD-003
tests.obligation: When a closed deterministic constant default is introduced on a table containing older rows, snapshot metadata MAY record one frozen fallback value for physically missing fields. That frozen value belongs to the field-introduction revision. Later edits to the default affect future insertions only.

tests.subject: ORNA-FIELD-004
tests.obligation: Future insertions logically store the evaluated default result. A storage profile MAY omit a value physically when it can reconstruct the row's already-frozen logical value without consulting a later declaration.

tests.subject: ORNA-FIELD-007
tests.obligation: A computed field is evaluated from the row under the current snapshot whenever observed and automatically reflects changes to its stored-field dependencies.

tests.subject: ORNA-FIELD-008
tests.obligation: A computed expression MUST be deterministic and row-local. It may read the current row and call pure helpers; it MUST NOT mutate tables, query unrelated tables, open streams, access secrets, perform I/O, or use ambient current time/randomness.

tests.subject: ORNA-FIELD-009
tests.obligation: Within a key-default or computed-field expression, each table field name is available as an immutable lexical selector of the prospective/current row, and `self` names the complete row context. A local binding may shadow a field only inside an explicitly nested block.

tests.subject: ORNA-FIELD-010
tests.obligation: Every stored/defaulted/computed field creates a selector such as `Contact.full_name`; `contact.full_name` applies it. Field dependencies appear in `sys.Dependency`.

tests.subject: ORNA-FIELD-011
tests.obligation: The planner MAY cache/materialize a computed selector, but this MUST NOT change its value, mutation rules, dependencies or serialization. Computed fields are excluded from standalone stored-row encoding unless a codec explicitly requests a derived projection.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-001
tests.obligation: `assert` is the only assertion-introducing keyword in Orna 1.0.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-002
tests.obligation: Assertions are enforced in all modes and MUST NOT be removed from release builds.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-006
tests.obligation: `all_unique(selector)` returns a predicate over a relation and tests uniqueness of the selector result according to its declared equality/null policy.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-007
tests.obligation: `every(predicate)` returns a predicate over a relation and is true only when the row predicate is true for every row.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-008
tests.obligation: The exact relation-predicate library is extensible through ordinary functions; adding one does not add assertion grammar.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-009
tests.obligation: A table assertion expression MUST type-check as `Predicate<Relation<Row>>` after owner-subject elaboration.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-010
tests.obligation: Table assertions are deterministic for a fixed candidate relation and captured database snapshot.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-011
tests.obligation: A table assertion MUST NOT perform network, process, UI or arbitrary filesystem effects, use nondeterministic randomness, or observe uncaptured wall-clock time.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-012
tests.obligation: Multiple assertions are conjunctive and evaluated in source order for deterministic diagnostics.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-018
tests.obligation: Dedicated table-field `unique` and `check(...)` modifiers are not 1.0 grammar. They migrate to table-owned `assert` predicates.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-019
tests.obligation: An assertion-specific `else` arm is invalid. Expected operational failure handling uses the ordinary failure/recovery model.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-020
tests.obligation: `ensure`, `check`, `fact`, `constraint`, `constraints`, dedicated `unique`, and `|!` are not aliases for `assert`.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-025
tests.obligation: Module assertions obey the same determinism and effect restrictions as table assertions.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-026
tests.obligation: A module assertion is evaluated whenever a validating boundary changes any table in its transitive dependency set.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-027
tests.obligation: Module assertions evaluate after all affected table-owned assertions and before publication of the candidate database.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-028
tests.obligation: Several applicable module assertions are ordered by owning module's stable ObjectId and then source span, providing deterministic first-failure behavior across modules.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-029
tests.obligation: A false module assertion aborts the complete candidate database boundary and rolls back all Orna-controlled writes in that boundary.

tests.subject: ORNA-KEY-003
tests.obligation: `Float` MUST NOT be accepted as a primary-key component.

tests.subject: ORNA-KEY-004
tests.obligation: A key's logical type MUST NOT be restricted to the host filesystem's native filename rules.

tests.subject: ORNA-KEY-005
tests.obligation: A stored table reference MAY be a key component when the referenced table key is permitted and canonically encodable. The path encodes the referenced row key, not an embedded row.

tests.subject: ORNA-KEY-006
tests.obligation: `Range<T>` is not a special overlap-identity key in version 1.0. If used as ordinary stored data, overlapping ranges are valid. A future temporal-exclusion feature must use an explicit, separately specified table constraint rather than redefining equality.

tests.subject: ORNA-MUT-001
tests.obligation: Rows are values; mutations are operations on tables.

tests.subject: ORNA-MUT-002
tests.obligation: Successful mutations MUST become visible in CWD atomically at the enclosing activation boundary.

tests.subject: ORNA-MUT-003
tests.obligation: Ordinary mutations MUST NOT automatically create a human Git commit unless an explicitly enabled publication policy publishes the accepted batch.

tests.subject: ORNA-MUT-004
tests.obligation: Primary keys MUST be immutable through ordinary `update`.

tests.subject: ORNA-MUT-005
tests.obligation: An explicitly keyed table MUST provide the ordinary table operation `Table.rekey(old_key, new_key)`. It changes one row's primary key atomically within the current activation.

tests.subject: ORNA-MUT-006
tests.obligation: `rekey` MUST fail without changing CWD when the old key is absent, the new key already exists, the new key is invalid, or deferred referential validation fails.

tests.subject: ORNA-MUT-007
tests.obligation: Referential constraints are validated at activation commit. A program MAY update dependent references and re-key the target in the same activation; no invalid intermediate state is observable outside that activation.

tests.subject: ORNA-MUT-008
tests.obligation: Non-optional references use `restrict` by default. Orna v1 does not perform an implicit cascade. A caller that wants dependent references changed MUST update them explicitly in the same activation.

tests.subject: ORNA-MUT-009
tests.obligation: Re-keying a table with the implicit automatic integer key is prohibited. Such an identity is never rewritten; create a new row and delete the old row instead.

tests.subject: ORNA-MUT-010
tests.obligation: `sys.Change` and semantic diff MUST represent a successful explicit re-key as one `rekey` change containing the old and new keys, even if its physical representation is a VFS directory change or a page replacement.

tests.subject: ORNA-MUT-011
tests.obligation: A raw filesystem path rename is not authoritative evidence of semantic continuity. Unless it corresponds to a pending explicit `rekey` intent, it is interpreted as deletion plus insertion; tooling MAY suggest the explicit operation but MUST NOT silently guess.

tests.subject: ORNA-OBJECT-004
tests.obligation: A manual unassisted rename that cannot be tied to committed identity metadata MUST be treated conservatively as delete plus create. Orna MAY offer explicit adoption but MUST NOT guess silently.

tests.subject: ORNA-OBJECT-005
tests.obligation: Retired IDs MUST NOT be reused for an unrelated definition.

tests.subject: ORNA-REF-003
tests.obligation: Non-optional references default to `restrict` on target delete or re-key. Weak/dangling references and automatic cascade are outside version 1.0.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-031
tests.obligation: An executable assertion evaluates its closed Boolean exactly once at the statement position.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-032
tests.obligation: A false executable assertion fails the activation with an `AssertionFailure` carrying the owning function, source span and safe values where available.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-034
tests.obligation: The implicit owner subject exists only during refined/table assertion elaboration and MUST NOT leak into nested ordinary declarations, closures, exports or stored values.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-035
tests.obligation: Assertion name resolution otherwise follows ordinary lexical/module resolution.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-036
tests.obligation: An empty `assert;` is invalid and receives `ORNA-A091-011`.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-037
tests.obligation: Every assertion clause ends with `;` and a missing terminator receives `ORNA-A091-005`.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-038
tests.obligation: A declaration assertion whose predicate type is incompatible with its owner receives `ORNA-A091-004` showing expected owner subject and actual type.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-039
tests.obligation: An effectful or nondeterministic declaration assertion receives `ORNA-A091-007` identifying the forbidden effect.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-040
tests.obligation: An implementation MAY stop after the first false assertion in deterministic order unless an explicit diagnostic mode requests all independent failures.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-045
tests.obligation: They run before graph publication, migration or a new physical root becomes visible.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-048
tests.obligation: Git snapshots, indexed row pages and the embedded unpublished tail are representations of one logical state and MUST NOT bypass assertions.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-050
tests.obligation: Assertion validation MUST preserve transaction atomicity and MUST NOT publish a state for which only a subset of applicable assertions ran.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-057
tests.obligation: Assertion failure MUST NOT be encoded as a hidden stored Boolean column, synthetic row or implicit index.

tests.subject: ORNA-ASSERT-058
tests.obligation: An optimizer MAY implement `all_unique`, `every` and cross-table predicates through indexes, anti-joins or incremental plans only when results and deterministic witnesses equal the reference logical evaluation.

tests.subject: ORNA-REL-001
tests.obligation: A relation value MUST remain composable without requiring full materialization.

tests.subject: ORNA-REL-002
tests.obligation: Relation presentation MAY request a bounded window of rows without enumerating the whole relation.

tests.subject: ORNA-ORDER-001
tests.obligation: A base table scan MUST be ordered by ascending canonical primary key.

tests.subject: ORNA-ORDER-002
tests.obligation: `filter` and one-to-one `map` preserve input order; `flat_map` uses input order followed by each produced value's order; `take`, `drop`, windows and `pairs` require/preserve order.

tests.subject: ORNA-ORDER-003
tests.obligation: `sort_by` establishes a stable order, `distinct` keeps the first occurrence, `union` yields left then right, grouped results use group-key order, and joins preserve left order with each right match in right-key order.

tests.subject: ORNA-ORDER-004
tests.obligation: An optimizer may reorder internally but MUST restore the declared observable order before values are observed.

tests.subject: ORNA-EQ-001
tests.obligation: Relation-wide `==` is invalid because sequence equality and set-of-rows equality are different operations. Libraries may provide explicitly named operations such as `same_sequence` and `same_rows`.

tests.subject: ORNA-QUERY-001
tests.obligation: A named live calculation MUST be an ordinary function rather than a `view` declaration.

tests.subject: ORNA-QUERY-002
tests.obligation: Calling the function evaluates its logical query against the current context unless arguments are explicitly snapshot-pinned.

tests.subject: ORNA-QUERY-003
tests.obligation: Two calls are not implicitly collapsed merely because their source spelling and arguments match. Effectful or nondeterministic calls execute independently.

tests.subject: ORNA-QUERY-004
tests.obligation: An implementation MAY reuse a previous call result only when the function is internally proven read-only and deterministic and its code, arguments, snapshot context, activation time and data dependencies have not changed. Reuse is an optimization, not a semantic guarantee.

tests.subject: ORNA-QUERY-005
tests.obligation: Writes performed earlier in the same activation participate in dependency invalidation and read-your-writes. A later call MUST observe those writes when its dependencies include the changed table.

tests.subject: ORNA-QUERY-006
tests.obligation: Actual reuse/materialization decisions SHOULD be visible through `sys.Materialization` and `orna explain` without requiring user effect annotations.

tests.subject: ORNA-HIST-004
tests.obligation: Values from different snapshot contexts MUST NOT be mixed implicitly.

tests.subject: ORNA-HIST-005
tests.obligation: If required historical Unicode, time-zone, codec or edition support is unavailable, Orna reports incomplete reproducibility rather than silently substituting current semantics.

tests.subject: ORNA-PLAN-001
tests.obligation: Materialization, caching, indexing and incremental maintenance MUST NOT change logical function results.

tests.subject: ORNA-PLAN-002
tests.obligation: Planner choices MUST be introspectable through `sys.Plan`, `sys.Storage`, `sys.Materialization` and `orna explain`.

tests.subject: ORNA-PLAN-003
tests.obligation: Every optimization MUST have a correct scan/reference fallback.

tests.subject: ORNA-CALL-003
tests.obligation: An implementation MAY evaluate an eligible call once and reuse the value. It MAY instead evaluate it repeatedly, provided the observable result and dependency context are identical.

tests.subject: ORNA-CALL-004
tests.obligation: When reuse/materialization occurs, `sys.Query`, `sys.Plan` or `sys.Materialization` MUST make the decision inspectable. The language does not promise a particular evaluation count for pure calls.

tests.subject: ORNA-DEP-001
tests.obligation: Dependencies MUST identify source and destination objects with typed `sys.Object` references.

tests.subject: ORNA-DEP-002
tests.obligation: Dependency kinds SHOULD include imports, calls, reads, writes, references, renders, uses-type and uses-unit.

tests.subject: ORNA-DEP-003
tests.obligation: Dependency information MUST be used for impact analysis, live invalidation, semantic diff, merge validation and selective testing where applicable.

tests.subject: ORNA-ATTACH-001
tests.obligation: Cross-database reads MAY compose relations from consistent snapshots of each attached database.

tests.subject: ORNA-ATTACH-002
tests.obligation: Orna MUST NOT claim atomic cross-database writes when attached databases have independent transaction logs.

tests.subject: ORNA-ATTACH-003
tests.obligation: Structural unit equivalence MUST be checked across database boundaries.

tests.subject: ORNA-PACKAGE-001
tests.obligation: Version 1.0 MUST NOT require a package registry, semantic-version solver or lockfile where exact Git commit pins already determine dependency state.

tests.subject: ORNA-PACKAGE-002
tests.obligation: Checking out an historical parent snapshot MUST resolve each attached database to the commit pinned by that snapshot.

tests.subject: ORNA-PACKAGE-003
tests.obligation: `std` remains an ordinary optional attached Orna database/library except for mandatory core language and `sys` facilities.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIB-001
tests.obligation: A program's library behaviour MUST be determined by its captured dependency snapshots. A historical program cannot silently substitute the currently installed `std` or current time-zone data.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIB-002
tests.obligation: Core integrity, transactions and assertions MUST work without `std`. An absent optional module produces the ordinary import diagnostic; it cannot be filled by an undocumented host library with the same spelling.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIB-003
tests.obligation: This section's portable operations MUST have the stated argument, order, failure and effect semantics when supplied under the reference-library profile. Other modules expose their exact public declarations through their pinned source and `sys`; their mere namespace name is not a claim of an unspecified portable API.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIB-004
tests.obligation: Read-only query callbacks MUST be effect-checked before optimisation. A relational plan may not hide an external side effect inside an expression that an optimiser could reorder, omit or repeat.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIB-005
tests.obligation: Failed callbacks propagate through the ordinary failure channel. A collection operator MUST NOT skip failed elements or substitute `null` unless that behaviour is requested by a separately named operation.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIB-006
tests.obligation: Mutation return values and missing-key behaviour MUST follow this table. Errors include the table identity and safe key, without disclosing redacted values. A failing operation's tentative writes cannot leak into the rest of the activation through a recovery handler.

tests.subject: ORNA-LIB-007
tests.obligation: The list-backed source MUST supply the complete declared identity, replay and preservation contract. It MUST NOT require an unprovided connector host or external account.

tests.subject: ORNA-TXN-007
tests.obligation: Orna MUST NOT imply that external effects are transactionally reversible.

tests.subject: ORNA-TXN-008
tests.obligation: User-visible effect annotations are not required for Orna to identify table mutations it owns. Internal effect information MAY be inferred for diagnostics, planning and introspection.

tests.subject: ORNA-TASK-001
tests.obligation: A child MUST NOT commit after the runtime has acknowledged its cancellation and terminal state. Lease fencing and transaction generation checks MUST enforce this when execution is hosted in a different process.

tests.subject: ORNA-TASK-002
tests.obligation: A graceful REPL close MUST cancel session-owned invocations and watches without terminating unrelated sessions or independently launched runs in the same runtime.

tests.subject: ORNA-TASK-003
tests.obligation: A hard process termination MUST NOT be described as executing cleanup in the dying process. A surviving runtime cancels work after loss of its owner lease; a restarted runtime recovers or rolls back open transactions before admitting writes. Committed changes remain durable.

tests.subject: ORNA-TASK-004
tests.obligation: The runtime MUST expose bounded cancellation checkpoints and adapter cancellation limitations. A task stuck in untrusted or noncooperative code cannot retain a writable transaction after its ownership lease has been revoked. An implementation may terminate an isolated worker to enforce this rule.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONCUR-004
tests.obligation: Programs requiring one atomic database update SHOULD perform concurrent read-only or external work first, then apply the combined table mutations in the parent activation.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONCUR-005
tests.obligation: `race` MUST return the first observed successful result, cancel and join all losers, and choose the lowest input-index ordinary failure if every child fails. Simultaneous successes use the runtime's recorded completion order; no wall-clock ordering between simultaneous events is promised.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONCUR-006
tests.obligation: `timeout` MUST request cancellation and join its child before failing with its timeout diagnostic. It never returns a successful partial value.

tests.subject: ORNA-CANCEL-002
tests.obligation: Interpreters, VMs, loops and stream operators MUST check cancellation at bounded execution points.

tests.subject: ORNA-BACKPRESSURE-001
tests.obligation: Stream channels MUST be bounded. A source that cannot be backpressured MUST declare or receive an explicit buffer, drop or fail policy before use.

tests.subject: ORNA-BACKPRESSURE-002
tests.obligation: `for_each` is sequential by default. Concurrent processing MUST be explicit, bounded and consistent with the connector's partition-order and checkpoint rules.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONSUMER-001
tests.obligation: Consumer identity is derived from database identity, the stable ObjectId of the invoked public function and canonical invocation arguments.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONSUMER-002
tests.obligation: The connector additionally supplies source identity, partition identity and position-format version. Secret plaintext MUST NOT participate in identity; a stable secret reference name may.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONSUMER-003
tests.obligation: Function code hashes are revisions, not identity. Editing or semantically renaming the function continues from the same checkpoint.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONSUMER-004
tests.obligation: Deleting and recreating a function creates a new consumer identity even when the spelling is reused.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONSUMER-005
tests.obligation: A durable consumer function containing more than one checkpointed source root MUST produce a diagnostic instructing the author to extract separate named consumer functions.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONNECTOR-001
tests.obligation: Source identity MUST be based on stable semantic configuration, not memory address, task order or AST position.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONSUMER-006
tests.obligation: One clone MUST prevent two local processes from concurrently owning the same consumer identity and partition.

tests.subject: ORNA-CONSUMER-008
tests.obligation: On merge, equal checkpoints merge. Opaque divergent positions create `sys.CheckpointConflict`; Orna MUST NOT choose a seemingly greatest opaque token.

tests.subject: ORNA-STREAM-003
tests.obligation: An unbounded stream consumer remains running until cancelled, failed or closed.

tests.subject: ORNA-STREAM-004
tests.obligation: Each item or configured ordered batch callback is a separate activation transaction; an unbounded consumer MUST NOT hold one transaction for its lifetime.

tests.subject: ORNA-STREAM-005
tests.obligation: Function values and anonymous functions have identical call semantics when used as stream/concurrency callbacks; wrapper lambdas MUST NOT be required where no arguments are captured.

tests.subject: ORNA-CP-002
tests.obligation: Publication MUST include checkpoint watermarks corresponding exactly to the included rows. It cannot publish a later watermark while omitting writes required by that watermark.

tests.subject: ORNA-CP-005
tests.obligation: Activation failure MUST roll back both table writes and checkpoint advancement.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-066
tests.obligation: Payload retention MUST obey the secret/redaction rules. A protected reference and digest may replace plaintext retention, but the exact source position remains part of delivery identity.

tests.subject: ORNA-CP-008
tests.obligation: A different clone MUST resume from the checkpoint present in its selected fetched snapshot, not a guessed local copy of another clone's tail.

tests.subject: ORNA-CP-009
tests.obligation: Recovery of unpublished data after machine loss requires replayable source data or a separately preserved local tail. Git replication alone does not contain unpublished state.

tests.subject: ORNA-PRES-001
tests.obligation: Implementations MUST NOT treat terminal presentation as canonical persistence encoding.

tests.subject: ORNA-PRES-002
tests.obligation: Inspect MUST expose type and structure, may truncate large collections, and MUST redact secret values.

tests.subject: ORNA-PRES-003
tests.obligation: Display MAY be lossy and contextual.

tests.subject: ORNA-PRES-006
tests.obligation: Every value has a host-derived, cycle-safe and bounded Inspect fallback.

tests.subject: ORNA-PRES-008
tests.obligation: Display/Present implementations are read-only, deterministic relative to their immutable context and subject to time/instruction/output budgets. Database writes, connectors, network, filesystem, process execution, secret reveal and nondeterministic time/randomness are unavailable.

tests.subject: ORNA-PRES-009
tests.obligation: A presenter failure falls back to Inspect with a diagnostic.

tests.subject: ORNA-PRES-010
tests.obligation: A renderer that does not recognize a rich node MUST fall back to an Inspect-compatible representation rather than fail to show the value.

tests.subject: ORNA-CODEC-001
tests.obligation: A codec MUST provide typed `encode(value)` and `decode(input, as: T)` operations.

tests.subject: ORNA-CODEC-002
tests.obligation: Decode MUST produce `T` on success or fail with a `DecodeError` preserving format location/path information. It MUST NOT wrap the successful value in `Result`.

tests.subject: ORNA-CODEC-003
tests.obligation: Canonical Orna encoding MUST be deterministic, full-precision, unambiguous and round-trippable for supported values.

tests.subject: ORNA-CODEC-004
tests.obligation: Generic value encoding of a table row MUST include all logical fields, including primary-key fields.

tests.subject: ORNA-CODEC-005
tests.obligation: Loading a row document MUST combine its admitted table schema, explicit/path key and decoded stored fields under the selected interchange/VFS context; arbitrary host paths cannot supply authority. Format-3 persistence encodes the key and stored fields directly through ORP-1.

tests.subject: ORNA-CODEC-006
tests.obligation: Exact checked-out source text MAY differ from canonical re-encoding because comments and formatting may be preserved. Exact source is obtained through `sys.File`, not by encoding the semantic value.

tests.subject: ORNA-PAGE-001
tests.obligation: Pages MUST be ordinary values returned by functions, not a separate component declaration grammar.

tests.subject: ORNA-PAGE-002
tests.obligation: Widgets and layouts MUST be ordinary values that can be composed by normal functions.

tests.subject: ORNA-WIRE-003
tests.obligation: The patch vocabulary is exactly `add`, `remove`, `replace` and `move`. Paths are typed sequences of record fields, relation keys and list indexes. A root replacement uses the empty path.

tests.subject: ORNA-WIRE-004
tests.obligation: Record children use field identity, relation rows use table `ObjectId` plus primary key, explicitly keyed UI children use that key, and unkeyed lists use position. Missing stable identity affects efficiency only; replacement MUST remain correct for every value.

tests.subject: ORNA-WIRE-005
tests.obligation: Connection queues, decoded message size, collection size, nesting depth and decompressed bytes MUST be bounded. A slow client MAY skip intermediate visual states and receive the newest complete snapshot. Database rows are not lost by visual coalescing.

tests.subject: ORNA-WIRE-006
tests.obligation: Reconnection does not require retained delta history. The client resubscribes and receives a complete current snapshot.

tests.subject: ORNA-WIRE-007
tests.obligation: A stale or unknown action handle MUST NOT execute. The host returns the current snapshot or a user-readable stale-view result.

tests.subject: ORNA-WIRE-008
tests.obligation: One action is one normal activation transaction. Successful writes commit together and invalidate watches; an escaping error or cancellation rolls them back.

tests.subject: ORNA-WIRE-009
tests.obligation: The binary envelope, message fields, deterministic CBOR rules and exact encodings for `Decimal`, `Money`, UUID/ObjectId, dates, instants, duration, quantities, enums, typed records, references, diagnostics and Present nodes are defined in `profiles/live-protocol.md` and form part of repository/server conformance.

tests.subject: ORNA-WIRE-010
tests.obligation: Secret values are not wire-encodable. A redacted secret handle may be presented only as non-revealing metadata.

tests.subject: ORNA-WIRE-011
tests.obligation: WebSocket compression is optional and cannot change semantics. Normal same-origin checks and the trusted authenticated VPN/SSH/reverse-proxy boundary apply; core Orna does not add a grants database.

tests.subject: ORNA-WIRE-012
tests.obligation: Protocol failures are rendered normally as user concepts such as “the live view was refreshed” or “this operation may already have completed.” Raw CBOR, revision or framing details appear only in explicit developer inspection.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-003
tests.obligation: User source MUST NOT declare, replace, shadow or monkey-patch the root `sys` namespace or any portable member specified in this chapter.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-010
tests.obligation: Portable names are case-sensitive. `sys.Table`, `sys.catalog.tables` and `sys.table` are not interchangeable spellings unless this specification explicitly defines them.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-006
tests.obligation: A conforming runtime MUST expose the compatibility fields of `sys.RuntimeInfo` in the [system reference](#system-reference), including exact language, system API, codec, storage and protocol coordinates; it MUST NOT claim a coordinate while omitting its required surface.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-007
tests.obligation: Unknown additive fields from a newer compatible `sys` minor version MUST be preserved or ignored safely according to the consumer's decoding mode; they MUST NOT be interpreted as a known field with a different meaning.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-008
tests.obligation: A consumer requiring an unavailable `sys` coordinate or profile MUST fail before performing writes.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-012
tests.obligation: A historical durable-system query MUST return exactly the observations retained by its snapshot. Known absence is an empty relation; pruned, missing or unhydrated data MUST be reported as unavailable, never substituted with observed emptiness.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-013
tests.obligation: A live `sys.rt` relation MUST NOT accept `as_of`. The implementation MUST direct callers to the corresponding durable relation when one exists.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-014
tests.obligation: CWD system relations MAY overlay newer local durable observations from Turso, but each row MUST identify whether it is committed, local-only or live-derived.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-015
tests.obligation: A historical row that states a run was `running` records the state observed at that snapshot; it MUST NOT imply that the process remains alive.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-022
tests.obligation: `sys.database.cwd` MUST remain stable for one evaluation snapshot and MUST change only at a defined transaction/snapshot boundary.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-023
tests.obligation: `sys.database.writable` reports whether the current attachment permits Orna-controlled writes; it does not assert that every later write will succeed.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-024
tests.obligation: Every function activation MUST observe one stable `sys.current.snapshot` unless it explicitly opens a nested operation whose API documents a new snapshot.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-027
tests.obligation: `sys.rt.id` identifies the current local owner/runtime generation and MUST change after an owner restart that invalidates prior live handles.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-028
tests.obligation: `sys.rt` MUST be available to every Orna command that opens a database, including direct embedded commands and commands temporarily coordinated through a local owner process.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-029
tests.obligation: `orna serve` MUST NOT be treated as the unique or authoritative `sys.rt`; it is one optional client/host mode over the same embedded-first database model.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-030
tests.obligation: Reads from `sys.rt` MUST be internally consistent to one observation instant or expose an `observed_at` field allowing the caller to detect a mixed observation.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-016
tests.obligation: Opaque system identifiers MUST compare by the identity they name, MUST have deterministic canonical encoding and MUST NOT be implicitly interchangeable with `Str`, `Uuid` or another identifier type.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-017
tests.obligation: A stable `sys.ObjectId` identifies one semantic object across ordinary edits and semantic renames; a `sys.RevisionId` identifies one immutable revision of that object.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-018
tests.obligation: Reusing an identifier for a semantically unrelated object is repository corruption and MUST be diagnosed by verification before publication.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-020
tests.obligation: A live handle presented to a different runtime owner MUST fail with `sys.handle.foreign_runtime`; it MUST NOT be treated as an identifier for a coincidentally equal live object.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-021
tests.obligation: Canonical serialization of a live handle MUST mark it non-resumable. Decoding it in a later process yields descriptive data, not an operational handle.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-025
tests.obligation: Child calls inherit locale, timezone, trace and cancellation context unless an explicit API parameter replaces one of them.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-026
tests.obligation: `sys.current.transaction` is present only when the activation participates in an Orna transaction. Its absence MUST NOT be represented by a fabricated zero identifier.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-031
tests.obligation: A state transition MUST follow the state machine specified for its row type; direct assignment of a state enum is not an administrative API.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-032
tests.obligation: A terminal invocation or run MUST NOT become non-terminal under the same execution identity; another execution has a new invocation/run identity. A durable failed-delivery identity follows the separate, versioned [delivery state machine](#checkpoints) and is preserved across attempts.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-033
tests.obligation: `qualified_name` is the name at the row's snapshot, not a timeless property of the stable object identity.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-034
tests.obligation: `semantic_hash` MUST exclude non-semantic formatting while `source_hash`, when present, identifies exact retained source bytes.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-036
tests.obligation: A generated definition MUST identify its generator/provenance where retained and MUST NOT be misreported as authored source.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-037
tests.obligation: Inferred types and inferred failure sets MUST be published in catalogue metadata exactly as if they had been written explicitly.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-038
tests.obligation: Catalogue metadata MUST retain whether an annotation was explicit so semantic tools can distinguish an annotation edit from an actual signature change.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-039
tests.obligation: Effect metadata MUST be a conservative superset of effects the function may perform; it MUST NOT omit a possible write, external effect or failure merely because an optimiser removed it in one build.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-040
tests.obligation: `sys.Table.assertions` MUST include every owner-scoped table assertion in source order and MUST expose the complete relation dependencies used for validation.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-041
tests.obligation: `sys.Assertion` MUST represent the contextual `assert` declarations specified by [assertions](#tables). A processor MUST NOT invent separate portable constraint/check/ensure/fact object kinds.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-042
tests.obligation: A table row count marked inexact MUST never be used as if it were an exact integrity fact.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-043
tests.obligation: Dependency traversal MUST be cycle-safe and deterministic.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-044
tests.obligation: A statically proven edge MUST use `exact` confidence. A conservative dynamic edge MAY use `possible`; tooling MUST NOT present `possible` as a proven call or write.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-045
tests.obligation: `sys.dependencies` and `sys.dependents` MUST preserve edge kind and source evidence rather than return only a set of names.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-046
tests.obligation: Diagnostic codes, primary spans and structured causes MUST remain available independently of a particular terminal or UI rendering.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-047
tests.obligation: Rendering a diagnostic MUST NOT mutate it, change its code or alter the underlying failure identity.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-048
tests.obligation: Secret values, decrypted source fragments, authorization material and unredacted connector payloads MUST NOT appear in diagnostic `message`, labels, causes, help, structured data, traces or presentation fallbacks.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-049
tests.obligation: A Git commit row and a semantic snapshot row MUST remain distinguishable even when they correspond one-to-one.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-050
tests.obligation: Hidden Orna refs MUST be visible through `sys.Ref.hidden` in explicit developer inspection and MUST remain valid ordinary Git refs.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-051
tests.obligation: A semantic diff MUST classify rename and rekey when identity evidence proves them; otherwise it MUST report conservative delete/add rather than invent identity.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-070
tests.obligation: Storage locations and host paths are sensitive metadata and MUST follow the path-redaction rules.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-071
tests.obligation: `sys.Secret` MUST never expose decrypted secret bytes, derived authorization headers or a value formatter that reveals them.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-096
tests.obligation: A portable failure code MUST retain its meaning throughout the 1.x compatibility line.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-097
tests.obligation: Implementations MAY add structured fields and vendor causes, but MUST NOT replace a required portable primary code with a vendor-only code.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-098
tests.obligation: Failure messages may be localized; code, structured fields and causal identity remain stable.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-053
tests.obligation: Explain output MUST be structured `sys.Plan` data. Human-readable tables or trees are `Present` renderings and are not the semantic result.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-054
tests.obligation: Actual execution counters MUST be absent when not measured; they MUST NOT be populated with estimates while marked actual.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-055
tests.obligation: A plan is snapshot-specific and MUST NOT be reused against a different schema revision without revalidation.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-056
tests.obligation: Every reflective `sys.invoke` or `sys.start` call MUST create an invocation identity before user code begins.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-057
tests.obligation: An unhandled ordinary failure MUST mark the invocation failed and roll back its Orna-controlled transaction before the failure is reported as terminal.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-058
tests.obligation: Cancellation MUST be recorded separately from ordinary failure and MUST bypass `|?` recovery inside the cancelled activation.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-059
tests.obligation: A run's `live` field is meaningful only for the current observation and MUST be false or absent in a purely historical projection.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-060
tests.obligation: Trace retention MAY be bounded, but the absence of discarded trace detail MUST be explicit and MUST NOT change invocation outcome.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-067
tests.obligation: Physical storage rows are introspection data and MUST NOT change the logical contents, ordering, equality or serialization of table rows.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-068
tests.obligation: A stored page MUST bind schema, logical key interval, generation and native object identity sufficiently to detect stale, overlapping or mismatched publication.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-069
tests.obligation: Missing lazily hydrated objects MUST be exposed as unavailable; a query may hydrate them according to policy but MUST NOT silently substitute incomplete results.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-072
tests.obligation: Build metadata MUST identify the complete source snapshot and compatibility coordinates used to produce an artifact.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-073
tests.obligation: A specification fixture listed as planned evidence MUST NOT be represented as passed unless an implementation actually executed it.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-074
tests.obligation: Every read/analysis function MUST return a normal typed value or relation that can be queried, encoded where supported and presented independently.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-075
tests.obligation: A root analysis function MUST NOT change checkout, refs, table contents, checkpoints, process state or retained failure state.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-076
tests.obligation: Name resolution and history functions MUST respect visibility and source redaction even in a trusted deployment.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-115
tests.obligation: `sys.Storage.profile` MUST identify the one recorded row profile; no new-format future-placement preference is exposed.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-116
tests.obligation: New-format admission MUST reject retired storage-preference functions rather than select a hidden legacy writer.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-117
tests.obligation: Physical maintenance MUST preserve every logical key/value, ordering and annotated Blob meaning; semantic row diff MUST be empty.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-118
tests.obligation: VFS path limits MUST be handled through reversible projection or explicit view errors, not by switching a table storage mode.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-119
tests.obligation: A maintenance stale-generation collision MUST preserve the prior authoritative root and report sys.storage.rewrite_conflict.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-120
tests.obligation: `sys.storage` is a grouping namespace, not a callable selector. Portable source MUST use `sys.Storage`, `sys.storage.objects` and the explicit `sys.admin` storage functions.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-084
tests.obligation: Direct mutation of a portable `sys` relation MUST fail at resolve/type-check time where statically evident and otherwise before any write is performed.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-085
tests.obligation: Every administrative function MUST define its transaction boundary, compare-and-set preconditions, failure codes and durable audit row.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-086
tests.obligation: An administrative function MUST validate all affected assertions before publishing its state transition.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-087
tests.obligation: A failed administrative operation MUST leave repository refs, logical CWD, checkpoints and runtime state at the last valid boundary described by its algorithm.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-088
tests.obligation: The 1.0 `sys.admin` boundary relies on OS/process isolation, Git/SSH credentials and the authenticated network perimeter; it MUST NOT be misrepresented as a built-in enterprise grants or role engine.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-089
tests.obligation: A continuation token MUST NOT be reused against a different snapshot, order, filter or redaction context.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-090
tests.obligation: Default iteration over an unordered system relation MUST NOT be documented as stable merely because one implementation happens to use object-ID order.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-091
tests.obligation: A multi-relation inspection operation requiring a coherent view MUST pin one observation snapshot/instant and expose it in the result.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-092
tests.obligation: A client that detects an observation-generation change during a live pagination sequence MUST restart or explicitly accept a new generation; rows MUST NOT be silently spliced across generations.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-093
tests.obligation: Retention policy MUST NOT delete data required to reproduce a committed logical snapshot while that snapshot remains advertised as complete.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-094
tests.obligation: Pruned optional detail MUST be represented as unavailable metadata, not as an empty value that could be mistaken for observed emptiness.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-095
tests.obligation: Retention and publication of runtime observations MUST never cause external effects or restart a program merely because a historical relation is queried.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-103
tests.obligation: A conformance claim MUST list every unavailable optional retention/detail profile but MUST NOT call a required portable member optional.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-104
tests.obligation: The conformance suite MUST test every root function with success, not-found/wrong-kind, snapshot, redaction and cancellation/failure cases applicable to that function.

tests.subject: ORNA-SYS-126
tests.obligation: The suite MUST prove one row writer, annotation-aware semantic identity, physical-rewrite neutrality and stale-generation rejection across Orna and VFS edits.

tests.subject: ORNA-ADMIN-001
tests.obligation: Every administrative call MUST record an invocation with the function, safe arguments, owner, observed generation and terminal outcome. State-changing calls MUST retain an audit event in the same local transaction as their durable transition, or in the recoverable journal for a Git transition. A failed call records failure without claiming that its requested state change occurred.

tests.subject: ORNA-ADMIN-002
tests.obligation: Administrative operations MUST NOT run reentrantly inside an activation holding uncommitted table writes. Such a call fails with `sys.admin.busy`; the caller may finish its transaction and submit administration as a new activation. Read-only planning and verification may inspect a pinned generation without mutating it.

tests.subject: ORNA-ADMIN-003
tests.obligation: A state-changing command MUST expose one of: no admission, admitted and recoverable, or terminal. On reconnect, an unknown outcome MUST be inspected through its retained invocation/journal identity before another non-idempotent command is issued.

tests.subject: ORNA-REPL-001
tests.obligation: The REPL MUST use ordinary `use` syntax for namespace access and MUST NOT require a separate `:cd` namespace model.

tests.subject: ORNA-REPL-002
tests.obligation: `$_` and `$?` are REPL bindings and MUST NOT become implicit globals in module source.

tests.subject: ORNA-REPL-005
tests.obligation: `:at` changes the default snapshot context for the session; it MUST NOT mutate repository HEAD.

tests.subject: ORNA-REPL-006
tests.obligation: `:watch` MUST use the same dependency and delta machinery as page sessions.

tests.subject: ORNA-CLI-001
tests.obligation: If Git already has the operation, Orna SHOULD preserve its name, flags and observable semantics. `orna mv` additionally preserves Orna semantic identity when the target is a definition or row key.

tests.subject: ORNA-CLI-002
tests.obligation: Runtime/checkpoint/failure detail and uncommon recovery operations SHOULD be available through typed `sys` values in the REPL and optional `std.devtools` pages.

tests.subject: ORNA-CLI-003
tests.obligation: `orna status --porcelain` MUST provide stable machine-readable output.

tests.subject: ORNA-CLI-004
tests.obligation: `orna status --short` SHOULD preserve Git's compact style while adding stable codes for runtime CWD summaries.

tests.subject: ORNA-DIAG-001
tests.obligation: Errors MUST have stable codes, concise titles, source spans when available, causes and actionable help where known.

tests.subject: ORNA-DIAG-002
tests.obligation: `orna explain <code>` SHOULD provide extended documentation.

tests.subject: ORNA-CLI-005
tests.obligation: Dynamic progress MUST be suppressed when output is not a terminal unless explicitly forced.

tests.subject: ORNA-UX-001
tests.obligation: Normal CLI output, REPL output, diagnostics, generated user documentation and default frontend text MUST describe the problem and remedy using Orna concepts.

tests.subject: ORNA-UX-002
tests.obligation: Normal user-facing output MUST NOT require the user to understand internal profile names, storage libraries, embedded-database terminology, wire encodings, object formats or extension ABI terminology.

tests.subject: ORNA-UX-003
tests.obligation: `--verbose` MAY provide additional Orna-level context. Raw implementation details require `--debug` or an equivalent explicitly technical interface.

tests.subject: ORNA-UX-004
tests.obligation: A diagnostic MUST lead with the user-visible condition and an actionable remedy. An implementation MAY attach machine-readable technical causes without rendering them by default.

tests.subject: ORNA-REPO-001
tests.obligation: `main.orna` MUST remain the fixed root module.

tests.subject: ORNA-REPO-004
tests.obligation: Stored rows MUST belong to stable reachable table identities in the format-3 store; rows are not individually imported modules or executable scripts.

tests.subject: ORNA-CORE-001
tests.obligation: Published repositories MUST use ordinary Git objects, refs and commits readable by ordinary Git tooling.

tests.subject: ORNA-CORE-002
tests.obligation: The implementation MUST NOT substitute a proprietary history graph, LFS, or a separate mandatory media service.

tests.subject: ORNA-CORE-003
tests.obligation: A published commit MUST bind complete source/schema/data/content closure and exact dependency gitlinks; local availability and globally complete snapshot identity MUST be distinguished.

tests.subject: ORNA-STATE-001
tests.obligation: `HEAD` MUST exclude uncommitted runtime data.

tests.subject: ORNA-STATE-004
tests.obligation: Explicit snapshots MUST resolve exactly, not silently rebind to a later branch head.

tests.subject: ORNA-STATE-004A
tests.obligation: Relation-level `as_of` MUST pin data and its decoding schema; whole-program historical execution is separately selected.

tests.subject: ORNA-META-001
tests.obligation: Format-3 tracked `.orna/` MUST contain only `database.orna` and `store`; required published system records MUST use the shared store.

tests.subject: ORNA-META-002
tests.obligation: `database.orna` MUST carry `repository_format: 3` and the stable database UUID; a separate `format.orna` is a legacy-format input, not another new-format authority.

tests.subject: ORNA-META-003
tests.obligation: Initialization MUST generate one UUIDv4, preserve existing source, and neither stage nor create a Git commit implicitly. Changing database identity requires an explicit fork-as-new-database migration.

tests.subject: ORNA-META-004
tests.obligation: Published checkpoint/allocator/runtime summaries MUST remain historical observations; checking them out MUST NOT rewind live fences, leases or non-rewindable allocators.

tests.subject: ORNA-META-005
tests.obligation: Caches, credentials, mounts, sessions, rejected edit drafts and unpublished changes MUST NOT be written into tracked `.orna/`.

tests.subject: ORNA-LOCAL-001
tests.obligation: Private state MUST use the per-worktree administrative path.
