tests.subject: ORNA-LOCAL-002
tests.obligation: Unpublished accepted state MUST be authoritative and crash-durable under the declared failure model.

tests.subject: ORNA-LOCAL-003
tests.obligation: Derived caches MUST be disposable and keyed by source/schema/store/interface generations.

tests.subject: ORNA-LOCAL-004
tests.obligation: Private state MUST never be added to ordinary commits or included by a naive working-directory copy advertised as a complete export.

tests.subject: ORNA-EMBED-001
tests.obligation: Local database use MUST work without devtools, a VFS mount, or `orna serve`.

tests.subject: ORNA-EMBED-002
tests.obligation: The local CLI MUST be able to own embedded state in-process when no local writer exists.

tests.subject: ORNA-EMBED-003
tests.obligation: Concurrent local commands MAY use private IPC to the single owner, not an obligatory public daemon.

tests.subject: ORNA-EMBED-004
tests.obligation: Correctness MUST NOT depend on experimental unsynchronized multi-process SQLite/Turso access.

tests.subject: ORNA-CLONE-001
tests.obligation: Clones and worktrees MUST have independent workspace/runtime identities; database UUID alone MUST NOT identify a writer.

tests.subject: ORNA-CLONE-002
tests.obligation: Published synchronization MUST use Git commits/fetch/push/merge.

tests.subject: ORNA-CLONE-003
tests.obligation: Non-fast-forward or concurrent writes MUST be explicit conflicts, not hidden cross-clone locks.

tests.subject: ORNA-CLONE-004
tests.obligation: Independent clones MUST NOT claim exactly-once external ingestion without a connector-specific coordination or idempotency contract.

tests.subject: ORNA-TURSO-001
tests.obligation: The local durable CWD MUST use embedded Turso/SQLite-compatible transaction storage, with no mandatory external server.

tests.subject: ORNA-TURSO-002
tests.obligation: Row writes and associated checkpoint/request outcomes MUST commit atomically in the owning local transaction.

tests.subject: ORNA-TURSO-003
tests.obligation: Implementations MUST document process/OS/power-loss guarantees, flush assumptions and measured settings.

tests.subject: ORNA-TURSO-004
tests.obligation: There MUST be at most one owning writable embedded state instance per worktree under the single-owner profile.

tests.subject: ORNA-TURSO-005
tests.obligation: Other local writers MUST coordinate with that owner or fail, never independently reopen an unsafe writable handle.

tests.subject: ORNA-TURSO-006
tests.obligation: Ownership acquisition/recovery MUST fence old writers before admitting a replacement.

tests.subject: ORNA-IMPL-001
tests.obligation: Git plumbing MAY use Git, gix or libgit2 while preserving native objects and observable Git semantics.

tests.subject: ORNA-BRANCH-001
tests.obligation: Creating a branch at HEAD MUST preserve CWD/index and create no implicit commit.

tests.subject: ORNA-BRANCH-002
tests.obligation: Selecting a branch at the same commit MUST preserve pending data, staged/unstaged source differences and non-rewindable continuity state.

tests.subject: ORNA-BRANCH-003
tests.obligation: A different-commit checkout MUST run CHECKOUT-3 with exact target validation, conflict preservation and recoverable state transitions.

tests.subject: ORNA-HOT-001
tests.obligation: High-rate writes MUST become durable and queryable in embedded Turso before publication.

tests.subject: ORNA-HOT-002
tests.obligation: Status output MUST summarise pending high-rate changes rather than emit one path per pending row.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-001
tests.obligation: The default compact writer target is 16 MiB of compressed data, with an 8–32 MiB normal tuning range and the compact profile's 64 MiB file bound. An implementation MAY choose a target within that range but MUST expose the effective policy. A changed tuning value does not change logical rows or checkpoint meaning.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-002
tests.obligation: A maximum pending age MAY cause publication of a smaller complete batch; the profile default is 60 seconds.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-003
tests.obligation: Publication policy MUST NOT introduce a different table declaration kind.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-004
tests.obligation: Effective policy and pending/published state MUST be visible through `sys.Storage` and runtime maintenance metadata.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-012
tests.obligation: Unresolved merges, rebases, overlapping managed-path edits or unreconcilable index state MUST pause automatic publication. Durable ingestion may continue within configured storage limits; exhaustion fails explicitly rather than discarding the tail.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-016
tests.obligation: Recovery MUST preserve unrelated staged and unstaged changes. An index lock left by a crashed publisher may be removed only after owner-liveness and journal checks establish that it is that publisher's abandoned lock.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-017
tests.obligation: A normal Git commit made after completed publication MUST not reverse published managed data unless the user explicitly staged such a reversal.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-013
tests.obligation: Graceful writer shutdown SHOULD publish eligible batches after its children have terminated and open activations have reached a boundary. A pending publication conflict does not justify discarding the local tail.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-014
tests.obligation: Status MUST report remaining unpublished CWD changes.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-015
tests.obligation: Transferring resumable execution to another clone requires publishing and pushing the recoverable state, then fetching the resulting snapshot in the receiving clone. Loss of an unpublished local tail can be repaired only by replayable source data or an independently preserved copy of that tail.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-018
tests.obligation: Pending graph objects MUST be native-pinned before mutation acknowledgement and remain protected through publication/recovery.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-019
tests.obligation: Auto-publication MUST be opt-in; the initial product defaults to explicit publication so successful saves do not silently create Git commits.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-020
tests.obligation: `.orna/store` index reconciliation MUST preserve separately staged logical changes and never stage the reverse of an automatically published batch.

tests.subject: ORNA-PUB-021
tests.obligation: Published system-watermark rows MUST be folded with the same batch without turning historical data into current operational authority.

tests.subject: ORNA-GIT-001
tests.obligation: A committed snapshot MUST identify all required local source, rows and content through native Git reachability and all dependencies through exact gitlinks/recorded origins.

tests.subject: ORNA-GIT-002
tests.obligation: Partial clones MAY defer blob payloads using ordinary filters and promisor remotes; unknown missing objects MUST be distinguished from promised objects.

tests.subject: ORNA-GIT-003
tests.obligation: A successful full/offline export MUST include all selected snapshot closure and recursive pinned dependencies, not just a pointer-only clone or mounted text files.

tests.subject: ORNA-GIT-004
tests.obligation: Fetch/push/clone MUST preserve Git compatibility and never require LFS to retrieve required content.

tests.subject: ORNA-GIT-007
tests.obligation: A full mirror of the superproject is not a complete submodule copy; export verification MUST recursively account for dependency object databases.

tests.subject: ORNA-GIT-008
tests.obligation: Refs required for allocator/consumer continuity MUST be synchronized with their existing ordering/validation rules; private edit/capture pins MUST NOT be exposed by ordinary push.

tests.subject: ORNA-GIT-010
tests.obligation: Collection MUST preserve content reachable from retained commits, local pins, pending accepted changes, open pins and unfinished recovery journals.

tests.subject: ORNA-GIT-011
tests.obligation: Repository clone credentials MUST be treated as access to repository content; VFS path hiding, namespaces or filtered clone are not row-level permissions.

tests.subject: ORNA-GIT-012
tests.obligation: Offline failure MUST name unavailable scope without exposing secrets; it MUST NOT silently use a current host file or another snapshot.

tests.subject: ORNA-EVOL-001
tests.obligation: Stable table/field identities MUST survive supported renames; a textual name match alone MUST NOT establish continuity.

tests.subject: ORNA-EVOL-002
tests.obligation: Schema changes MUST be admitted against affected rows, references, assertions, indexes and stored codecs before visibility.

tests.subject: ORNA-EVOL-003
tests.obligation: Historical rows MUST be decoded under their historical schema/value profile; current source MUST NOT silently reinterpret them.

tests.subject: ORNA-EVOL-004
tests.obligation: Semantic diff MUST compare logical fields and Blob annotations/content, not storage page or Git-layout IDs.

tests.subject: ORNA-EVOL-005
tests.obligation: A three-way merge MUST validate the merged program/schema/data/content closure and constraints before publishing; a conflict-free Git text merge is not sufficient.

tests.subject: ORNA-EVOL-006
tests.obligation: Conflicting replacements of one Blob MUST be reported as value conflicts unless an explicit application merge function supplies a validated replacement; concatenating chunk lists is not a default merge.

tests.subject: ORNA-EVOL-007
tests.obligation: Explicit rekey MUST use normal immutable-key/reference rules and emit one logical rekey with old/new address, not a filename guess.

tests.subject: ORNA-EVOL-008
tests.obligation: A representation-only rewrite MUST preserve semantic rows and content commitments. Defaulting new annotations in migration is an explicit semantic migration, not falsely an empty semantic diff.

tests.subject: ORNA-EVOL-009
tests.obligation: Required introduction defaults/fallbacks MUST be frozen under the source/schema revision rather than reevaluated on every historical read.

tests.subject: ORNA-EVOL-010
tests.obligation: A failed migration/merge/checkout MUST preserve accepted state and conflicting user edits; no automatic ref reset, inferred winner or unknown-schema overwrite is allowed.

tests.subject: ORNA-TRUST-003
tests.obligation: Public anonymous mutation or arbitrary remote REPL execution is outside the trusted v1 profile.

tests.subject: ORNA-EXT-003
tests.obligation: A Wasm extension MUST NOT receive raw pointers/handles to Turso or Git internals. Host calls use typed interfaces so a trap cannot corrupt repository/runtime memory.

tests.subject: ORNA-EXT-004
tests.obligation: Implementations SHOULD enforce coarse execution budgets and cancellation for portable components. These controls bound execution; they do not grant per-device permissions.

tests.subject: ORNA-EXT-005
tests.obligation: Native extensions run with the host process's trust and MUST be labeled as such. Orna does not sandbox native extensions.

tests.subject: ORNA-SECRET-001
tests.obligation: Orna MUST NOT commit plaintext secret values by default.

tests.subject: ORNA-SECRET-002
tests.obligation: Secret values MUST be redacted from Inspect, Display, Present, diagnostics, traces and `sys` unless an explicitly privileged operation requests disclosure.

tests.subject: ORNA-SOPS-001
tests.obligation: An SOPS provider MUST decrypt in memory and SHOULD avoid writing plaintext temporary files.

tests.subject: ORNA-SECRET-003
tests.obligation: A `SecretRef` may be displayed and serialized by stable name; the resolved secret value may not.

tests.subject: ORNA-SERVE-001
tests.obligation: `orna serve` provides Git transport, page/query endpoints and WebSocket presentation deltas for its clone.

tests.subject: ORNA-SERVE-005
tests.obligation: Core Orna does not define principals, groups, grants, per-device roles or row-level permissions.

tests.subject: ORNA-SERVE-007
tests.obligation: Git transport MUST remain usable when the optional Git/database web frontend is absent.

tests.subject: ORNA-SERVE-008
tests.obligation: The default frontend SHOULD be an ordinary, removable devtools application. An upstream `std.devtools` package or a vendored `devtools` module is permitted; neither name is privileged. The minimal source-hosted profile and exact source/resource ownership are defined in [source-hosted applications](#source-apps).

tests.subject: ORNA-SERVE-009
tests.obligation: When installed as `/`, the default frontend SHOULD lead with database tables and also expose files, commits, branches, functions, dependencies, storage and runtime state.

tests.subject: ORNA-FORMAT-001
tests.obligation: Each canonical encoder MUST use the exact selected profile. OVB-1 legacy/wire encodings remain unchanged; OVB-2 uses the additions below. Strict decoders MUST reject aliases and foreign-profile tags before identity use.

tests.subject: ORNA-FORMAT-002
tests.obligation: A CWD reference MUST identify its captured generation. A context-free `[0]` is invalid. A decoder unable to resolve a pin MUST report `sys.snapshot.expired` or `sys.snapshot.incomplete`; it MUST NOT rebind the reference to current CWD.

tests.subject: ORNA-FORMAT-003
tests.obligation: A referenced database, type, table and key schema MUST agree. Decoding data from another snapshot does not implicitly import its schema or replace the current execution context.

tests.subject: ORNA-FORMAT-004
tests.obligation: Canonical text decoding MUST be type-directed and non-executable. It MUST distinguish optional absence, scalar values, row references and nominal construction according to the supplied schema, and validate all refinements before returning a value.

tests.subject: ORNA-FORMAT-005
tests.obligation: New annotated Blob values MUST preserve annotations through OVB-2 and MUST NOT silently lose them on old wire/export interfaces.

tests.subject: ORNA-FORMAT-006
tests.obligation: Stored and semantic reference tags MUST be rejected outside their recorded ROV-3/SOV-3 contexts; a raw SHA or Git OID is never permission to read content.

tests.subject: ORNA-PROTO-001
tests.obligation: An implementation MUST decode and validate the complete message, required fields, canonical forms and configured limits before admitting its operation. It MUST reject duplicate map keys and noncanonical integer/length forms; it MUST NOT execute a partially decoded request.

tests.subject: ORNA-PROTO-002
tests.obligation: Session resumption MUST preserve request reservations and terminal outcomes for that session while its lease remains valid. A new runtime generation MUST invalidate operational handles from the old generation. Durable request recovery may report old outcomes as data without reviving old handles or owners.

tests.subject: ORNA-PROTO-003
tests.obligation: The client MUST apply the ordered operations to a temporary tree and publish them atomically only if its current revision equals the declared base and every operation succeeds. Otherwise it MUST discard the patch and request resynchronisation. It MUST NOT leave a partially patched visible tree.

tests.subject: ORNA-PROTO-004
tests.obligation: A durable admission reservation and a terminal transactional claim are distinct records/states. The terminal claim and successful Orna writes MUST share one transaction. A reservation without a terminal claim MUST NOT be treated as permission to execute a potentially effectful request again.

tests.subject: ORNA-TEST-001
tests.obligation: Every valid language fixture requires successful parse, name resolution and type checking. Parser-only success MUST NOT be presented as full validity.

tests.subject: ORNA-TEST-002
tests.obligation: Every invalid fixture identifies the expected failing phase and stable diagnostic code.

tests.subject: ORNA-TEST-004
tests.obligation: Bundle validation distinguishes: a test is specified, a test exists in an implementation, and a test passed. Document/index checks MUST NOT claim that Orna source executed when no implementation was run.

tests.subject: ORNA-TEST-005
tests.obligation: The corpus covers each normative syntax alternative, precedence boundary and deliberately invalid ambiguous form. It need not manufacture a positive and negative file for every mechanical EBNF helper production.

tests.subject: ORNA-TEST-006
tests.obligation: A generated requirement-to-test coverage report SHOULD expose untested normative behaviour, but it MUST remain a reporting layer over ordinary tests rather than a new test language or CI system. Informative rationale is excluded from the denominator.

tests.subject: ORNA-TEST-009
tests.obligation: `tests/conformance-manifest.json` MUST index valid, invalid and complete-project fixtures. A complete-project fixture MUST include `load_rows`, which admits the supplied fixture rows through their declared legacy input reader, validates them against the resolved schema/units, then imports them into the current row engine; fixture files do not enable a second new-format row writer.

tests.subject: ORNA-TEST-010
tests.obligation: `tests/requirement-evidence.json` MUST attach a non-empty `tests` list to every numbered requirement. Entries may name ordinary source fixtures, project fixtures, vector suites, behavioural/fault scenarios, interoperability suites, benchmark suites or an explicit inspection requirement. The mapping is a test plan, not evidence that an implementation has executed it.

tests.subject: ORNA-TEST-011
tests.obligation: Machine-testable normative behaviour MUST be identified as requiring an executable fixture, vector, project, scenario or implementation suite. A plan without an implemented test remains unexecuted. Bundle validation MUST fail when a requirement has no recorded evidence obligation; production conformance additionally requires the applicable implementation evidence to pass.

tests.subject: ORNA-TEST-007
tests.obligation: Test tooling SHOULD support temporary branch/worktree isolation without requiring a separately administered test server.

tests.subject: ORNA-TEST-008
tests.obligation: Branch-based tests MUST NOT imply that mocks or conventional unit tests are forbidden; the branch model is an integration-state primitive, not a ban on other testing methods.

tests.subject: ORNA-EVIDENCE-001
tests.obligation: A release report MUST distinguish authored conformance cases from executed implementation evidence and MUST NOT infer a pass from a filename, requirement association, file count or manifest validity.

tests.subject: ORNA-EVIDENCE-002
tests.obligation: A complete example project MUST include every required module/schema or pin an available dependency with an exact interface. Placeholder connector attachment points do not make an example self-contained.

tests.subject: ORNA-CLOSURE-002
tests.obligation: Benchmark, cross-platform, interoperability, security and fault obligations determine an implementation's evidence for its claimed profile. They MUST NOT be used as permission to choose different observable semantics.

tests.subject: ORNA-CLOSURE-003
tests.obligation: Features outside the declared language/profile are absent, not implicitly implementation-defined. A source program relying on such a feature MUST receive an unsupported-feature or resolution diagnostic rather than silently acquiring vendor-specific behaviour under the same portable coordinate.
